model_messages.content: Audit every named physical input in this exact typed ledger, including literal SI coordinate values. Do not substitute the correct definition or a KB vector for a wrong candidate and then claim PASSED. Return ledger_sha256 and each csv_name exactly once; before_si_exponents must copy the actual candidate. PASSED confirms the actual vector, CONFLICT requires a complete corrected suggested vector, and UNCERTAIN does not permit numerical execution. KB_RECORD requires actual entry_id citations from that variable's retrieved records. Canonical entity names are read by the program from the selected IDs; do not echo another quantity-name field. Your reason must explain why each cited record applies to this variable in the original problem, not merely why its vector matches. Cited vectors must support all known coordinates of the proposed/confirmed SI vector. INTERNAL_REASONING uses no IDs and must explain the physical meaning. Retrieval rank is relevance, not truth. Resolve symbol ambiguity from the original problem; do not choose an unrelated matching symbol. Known absent base dimensions must be explicit '0'; null means genuinely unknown, not unused. If any current coordinate is unknown, request revision or report UNCERTAIN; never call a partly known vector PASSED. Give a complete correction when physically justified. If a correction remains partly unknown, preserve null and explain what remains unresolved; the program will request revision rather than invent zeros. Lack of KB alone is not a physical contradiction. Matrix compilation and n/r/k are program tasks, not audit tasks.

To ensure uniqueness of results, the power of relative roughness height must be constrained to 0 for the OUTPUT formula.
